Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `WordUtilsTest.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/local_workplace/commons-text/src/test/java/org/apache/commons/text/WordUtilsTest.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

Now I'll write the improved, more understandable version of the test, preserving all behavior.Compilation succeeded (`COMPILE_OK`; the deprecation note is from the original `isDelimiter` tests and is expected).

I refactored `WordUtilsTest.java` for understandability while preserving exact runtime behavior — every method is still called with the same arguments and the same expected outcomes. Key improvements:

- **Logical grouping**: tests reordered and separated by the CUT method they exercise (`abbreviate`, `capitalize`, `capitalizeFully`, `containsAllWords`, `initials`, `isDelimiter`, `swapCase`, `uncapitalize`, `wrap`, regressions, constructor) with section banners.
- **`@DisplayName` on every test** describing the intent in plain language.
- **Explanatory inline comments** clarifying non-obvious cases (whole-word matching, `upper == -1` meaning "no limit", suffix-only-when-shortened, leading/trailing space handling, locale independence, etc.).
- **Clearer naming**: the generic `chars`/`array` locals are renamed to `delimiters`.
- **Self-documenting surrogate-pair constants** (`GOTHIC_A`, `GOTHIC_DELIM_1`, …) replacing raw `\uD800\uDFxx` escapes — same code points, just readable. The char-array delimiters are derived from those constants (`GOTHIC_DELIM_1.toCharArray()`), yielding identical arrays.
- Inline `\u01C8`/`\u01C9` escapes in `swapCase` replaced with the actual title/lower-case characters (identical values, UTF-8 source).
